Although automated analysis indicates the project is up to standards, the manual review reveals critical misconfigurations in the Electron sandbox environment. The most concerning issues involve the bypass of Electron's security model. The implementation effectively forces 'nodeIntegration' to true while disabling 'contextIsolation', which exposes the host machine to arbitrary code execution risks. Additionally, a logic error in file cleanup during download cancellation will likely cause the main process to crash when attempting to remove files using directory-specific commands. The CI pipeline is currently limited to linting. To ensure the stability of this major version jump, it is recommended to integrate functional tests that validate the newly migrated Promise-based APIs and crash handling logic. #### About this PR - The PR explicitly disables Electron security warnings while maintaining 'nodeIntegration: true'. This contradicts modern Electron security best practices and should be revisited alongside the contextIsolation configuration. - The new CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) only executes linting. Given the migration from legacy callback APIs to Promises and the move to Electron 29, functional tests (using the existing Mocha/Chai setup) should be integrated into the pipeline to prevent regressions.

items.author: Copilot
items.body: This promise-based call will throw `TypeError: mkdirp is not a function` at runtime. With mkdirp v3, the default CommonJS import (`const mkdirp = require('mkdirp')` in `index.js`, which `build-tweaks.js` shares via the global script scope) resolves to a namespace object of named exports, not a callable function. That is why the other call sites in this file use `mkdirp.sync(...)` (the `sync` named export) and continue to work, but calling `mkdirp(...)` directly does not. Because the error is thrown synchronously before a promise is returned, the `.catch()` here won't handle it, and `buildTweaksConfig()` will never run — breaking the compile flow. Use the callable async export `mkdirp.mkdirp(...)` (or `mkdirp.sync(...)`), or change the import in `index.js` to `const { mkdirp } = require('mkdirp')` (the function still carries a `.sync` method).
